subject: Palisade security questionnaire: residency & retention details for Hosted API
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@palisade.com>

Cc: Maya Conway <maya.conway@palisade.com>, security@palisade.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security questionnaire — residency, retention, deletion specifics

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our short security questionnaire (Palisade SQ v3) — the two priority items for our procurement team are: 1) where customer request/response data is stored for the Hosted API (region/fallbacks) and 2) how long request logs / full responses are retained, and the timeline/process for permanent deletion on request.

High level questions: can you confirm default region(s) for Hosted API, whether we can force EU-only storage for a specific account, and the SLO for a verified deletion request? We also need a short attestation we can include in our vendor risk review.

Would appreciate a written reply we can attach to the RFI.

Regards,
Sam

Head of InfoSec — Palisade Financial

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — residency, retention, deletion specifics

Hi Sam — thanks, and welcome. Quick summary below (I put a one-page PDF attached for your risk team). I'm looping in Neha (Security) and Ben (Infra) for technical confirmation; Soojin for contractual follow-up if you want this captured as an addendum.

Summary (hosted API):
- Default datastore region: US (us-east) for new self-serve accounts.
- EU region: available by request/accounts can be region-pinned to EU (data and primary backups kept in eu-west region). Region-pinning is an enterprise configuration; we can scope it per-account or per-tenant.
- Request/response retention: Default: 30 days for full request/response payloads (used for debugging and support). Metadata (request headers, token usage for billing and metrics) is retained for up to 365 days.
- Caches & ephemeral state: KV caches and per-request model state are ephemeral and not written to long-term storage; most are evicted within 24 hours and never copied to persistent backups.
- Deletion workflow: Verified deletion (data egress + purge of request/response payloads) begins on confirmation and is typically completed within 72 hours; final audit trace kept for 90 days (audit traces are metadata-only, e.g., deletion event id, operator id, no customer payload).
- Encryption & key management: All hosted data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.3). Customer data in hosted accounts is encrypted with service KMS; for Enterprise we support customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM).

Next steps we can offer: official attestation letter (signed), an EU-only addendum for account region-locking, and a sample redaction report once deletion completes. See attached one-pager.

If you want, Neha will add a technical appendix with log locations, key rotation cadence, and backup retention.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-retention-summary.pdf (one-page summary)

On 2026-05-18 11:03, Jasmine Liu wrote:
> Summary (hosted API):
> - Default datastore region: US (us-east) for new self-serve accounts.
> - EU region: available by request/accounts can be region-pinned to EU (data and primary backups kept in eu-west region).

Adding the technical appendix (detailed answers for Palisade SQ):

1) Precise residency behavior
- Primary storage: customer request and generated content is stored in the account's primary region (us-east or eu-west) depending on region-pin.
- Fallbacks: transient cross-region replication is disabled for region-pinned enterprise accounts. For standard hosted accounts we maintain multi-region read-replicas for availability; replicas contain only metadata and are removed within 48h if account is region-switched.

2) Retention buckets and timelines (concrete)
- Full request/response payloads (debug logs): default TTL = 30 days, stored encrypted, purged automatically by retention job.
- Billing/metrics metadata (token counts, endpoints called, timestamps): retained 365 days for invoicing/analytics.
- Audit logs (operator actions, deletion events): stored 90 days (metadata only).
- Backups/snapshots: backups retained 90 days; snapshots are region-scoped and encrypted.

3) Deletion process and verification
- Customer initiates deletion via support portal or API (official request + identity verification).
- Deletion workflow: flag account → remove payloads from primary storage (background job) → remove backups related to payloads → write deletion audit event.
- SLA: standard hosted accounts: purge completes within 72 hours after verification. Enterprise accounts can contract a 24–48 hour SLA and an on-demand escrow for proofs.
- Verification artifacts: we provide a signed deletion certificate (contains deletion job id, timestamps, operator id) and a short redaction sample (we do not provide raw erased payload).

4) Encryption & key management
- Keys: service uses AES-256; keys stored and rotated in our KMS with 90-day rotation for root service keys and 30-day rotation for session keys.
- Customer-managed keys: available for enterprise; KMS logs can be exported on request (subject to contract).

5) Limits & exceptions
- For accounts with regulated workloads (e.g., EU financial customers) we recommend region-pinning + CMK.
- Note: retention for backups and billing metadata (365d) is necessary for invoicing and legal record-keeping; contractual exceptions are possible but require negotiation.

Attached is a redacted audit log sample to show the deletion event format. Happy to add more specifics into the form if Palisade needs row-level answers.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
